# Resource: catalyst_function_cron

Manage a pre-defined CronExpression, daily/monthly/yearly calendar, one-time or relative periodic schedule targeting an existing Job Function and Function Job Pool. Validates target identities and project membership before writes. Defaults to disabled. Enabling submits real jobs and may incur Catalyst usage. The Function code and pool are separate resources/prerequisites. Supports updates, import as project_id/cron_id, drift and confirmed deletion. Requires cron create/read/update/delete, jobpool read, Function read and project read scopes. Parameter values are sensitive but remain in Terraform state; secure your state storage. Set exactly one schedule mode. Time and form changes update the same cron ID; date/week forms clear omitted fields. Week-based calendars require one weekday. One-time timestamps use Unix seconds and omit end_time. Relative interval_seconds schedules use UTC and recurring end_time; elapsed intervals omit the wall-clock timezone from API requests. Legacy Cron Function triggers are not managed here. Live validation is limited to India Development.

## Environment Isolation

An explicit provider organization is required. The computed `routing_scope` binds
this resource to its data center, environment and organization. Changed routing is
rejected before resource API calls, including when applying a saved creation plan.
Refresh legacy state under its original routing before updating or deleting it.
See [environment isolation and migration](../guides/environments.md).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "catalyst_function_cron" "example" {
  project_id  = var.project_id
  job_pool_id = var.function_pool_id
  function_id = var.job_function_id
  name        = "terraform_function_cron"
  job_name    = "terraform_job"
  expression  = "0 0 * * *"
  timezone    = "Asia/Kolkata"
  end_time    = var.end_time
  enabled     = false
  params      = {}
}
```

## Argument Reference

### Required

- `function_id` (String) Existing Job Function ID in the same project. This is a Job Function (type job), not a legacy Cron Function.
- `job_name` (String) Job name: 1–20 ASCII letters, digits or underscores. Hyphens were rejected by the live Function scheduling API.
- `job_pool_id` (String) Existing Function Job Pool ID in the same project.
- `name` (String) Unique cron name in the project.
- `project_id` (String) Existing project ID. Changing it replaces the cron.

### Optional

- `calendar_schedule` (Attributes) Daily, monthly or yearly calendar schedule, using the resource timezone. Choose dates or weeks/weekdays for monthly/yearly schedules. Mutually exclusive with expression, one_time_at and interval_seconds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--calendar_schedule))
- `description` (String) Cron description. Defaults to an empty string.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the cron submits jobs. Defaults to false; set true deliberately to activate the schedule.
- `end_time` (Number) Required positive end timestamp in Unix seconds for recurring schedules. Omit for one-time schedules; the API end sentinel is computed.
- `expression` (String) Five-field cron expression. Set exactly one of expression, calendar_schedule, one_time_at or interval_seconds.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Positive relative repetition interval in seconds. Recurring end_time is required. Relative intervals use the default UTC and omit the wall-clock timezone from API requests. Select exactly one schedule mode.
- `one_time_at` (Number) One-time execution Unix timestamp in seconds. Omit end_time for this mode; use a future timestamp when enabling. Select exactly one schedule mode.
- `params` (Map of String, Sensitive) Complete string parameter map passed to the Job Function. Defaults to an empty map.
- `retry_count` (Number) Number of retries for failed jobs. Defaults to zero; Catalyst validates its service limits.
- `retry_interval` (Number) Retry interval in seconds. Use 60 to 86400 seconds with retry_count greater than zero; otherwise leave zero.
- `timezone` (String) IANA wall-clock timezone for expression/calendar/one-time schedules; defaults to UTC (encoded as the API GMT timezone). Periodic intervals use UTC because they measure elapsed time.

## Attribute Reference

- `id` (String) Cron ID as an exact numeric string.
- `routing_scope` (Attributes) Saved data center, environment and explicit organization routing. Provider routing must match before reads, plans or mutations. Legacy state binds only after a successful refresh with the original routing. This records configuration, not authenticated caller identity. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routing_scope))

<a id="nestedatt--calendar_schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `calendar_schedule`

Required:

- `hour` (Number) Hour of day, 0–23 in timezone.
- `minute` (Number) Minute, 0–59.
- `repetition` (String) daily, monthly or yearly.
- `second` (Number) Second, 0–59.

Optional:

- `days` (Set of Number) Dates in the month, 1–31. Use dates or the weeks/weekdays pair. Defaults to an empty set.
- `months` (Set of Number) Months: 1 is January and 12 is December. Required for yearly schedules; omit for daily/monthly. Defaults to an empty set.
- `week_days` (Set of Number) Exactly one weekday: 1 Sunday, 2 Monday, 3 Tuesday, 4 Wednesday, 5 Thursday, 6 Friday, 7 Saturday. Multiple weekdays are rejected by the service. Supply with weeks_of_month, instead of days. Defaults to an empty set.
- `weeks_of_month` (Set of Number) Weeks, 1–5. Supply with week_days, instead of days. Defaults to an empty set.


<a id="nestedatt--routing_scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routing_scope`

Read-Only:

- `data_center` (String)
- `environment` (String)
- `organization_id` (String)

## Import

Use the same provider data center, organization and environment as the existing
resource. Import reads the object into state; review the next plan before apply.

### Import Command

```shell
terraform import catalyst_function_cron.example 'PROJECT_ID/CRON_ID'
```
